query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a 1-2 μm thick alumina (Al2O3) coating via plasma electrolytic oxidation to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: 1-2 μm thick alumina (Al2O3) coating via plasma electrolytic oxidation
generation.conditions: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 100 hours, Mechanical-loading boundary: 500 MPa
generation.mechanism: The alumina coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing the formation of embrittling oxides and thereby preserving the alloy's ductility [no specific record ID available due to empty list].
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20-30% increase in room-temperature tensile ductility and a 10-20% decrease in yield strength at 1000 °C compared to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr
generation.boundary: Temperature: 1000 °C, Atmosphere: Air, Exposure time: 100 hours, Mechanical-loading boundary: 500 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance may vary depending on the coating quality, thickness, and uniformity, as well as the specific testing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled exposure of coated and uncoated cast HfNbTaTiZr samples to 1000 °C in air for 100 hours, followed by room-temperature tensile testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples exhibit less than 10% increase in room-temperature tensile ductility or more than 30% decrease in yield strength at 1000 °C compared to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the hypothesis is falsified.
